etymology.text: Ideogrammic compound: 大 ‘man’ + 口 ‘mouth, opening’ (interpretations differ). Its oldest meaning is ‘to leave, to depart from’; ‘to go to’ developed from it.

funFacts: 去年 ‘the year that has gone’ is ‘last year’: 去 keeps its old meaning ‘to leave’ there.
去声 ‘the departing tone’ is the traditional name of the 4th tone — and 去 qù itself is said in the 4th tone.
pitfalls: 去 takes the place directly: 去学校 ‘go to school’ — no word for ‘to’ (*去到学校 is not needed, *去在学校 is wrong).
去 is movement away from where you (or the listener) are; towards the speaker it is 来: 你来我家吧 ‘come to my place’.
subtleties: ‘Go and do’ has two orders: 去超市买牛奶 and 买牛奶去 — the first is the everyday one.
After another verb 去 shows the direction away: 进去 ‘go in (there)’, 出去 ‘go out’, 回去 ‘go back’ — the 去 is then often toneless.

etymology.text: Pictogram of wheat (the original of 麦 ‘wheat’): ear, leaves and roots. The character was borrowed for the word ‘to come’ already in the oracle bones.

funFacts: 来 was first a drawing of wheat; ‘wheat’ later got its own character 麦, and 来 kept ‘come’ — a sound loan more than 3000 years old.
pitfalls: 来 is movement towards the speaker — or towards the listener: answering someone who calls you, ‘coming!’ is 来了！; going somewhere neither of you is, it is 去.
从来 is not ‘from … come’: it is the adverb ‘ever / never’ (S08). In 他从北京来 the place stands between 从 and 来.
subtleties: After a verb 来 says the movement comes this way: 进来 ‘come in (here)’ vs 进去 ‘go in (there)’ — the speaker’s position decides.
In requests 来 stands for almost any verb: 来一碗米饭 ‘a bowl of rice, please’.

etymology.text: Ideogrammic compound: 門 ‘door’ + 一 ‘latch’ + 廾 ‘a pair of hands’ — two hands opening a latched door. The simplified 开 keeps only the latch and the hands.

etymology.text: Ideogrammic compound: 留 + 土 ‘ground’ — staying on the ground. Sino-Tibetan; cognate with Tangut and Japhug words for ‘to sit’.

funFacts: In the modern character you can see two people (人 人) sitting on the ground (土) — an easy way to remember it, though the old form was 留 + 土.
pitfalls: You 坐 a vehicle you ride inside as a passenger (bus, train, plane, taxi, boat), you 骑 what you sit astride (bicycle, horse, motorbike), and you 开 what you drive.
坐 + vehicle comes before the main verb: 我坐火车去北京 ‘I go to Beijing by train’ — 我去北京坐火车 means ‘I go to Beijing to take a train’.
subtleties: The vehicle phrase answers 怎么去？ ‘how do you get there?’: 坐公共汽车 / 坐地铁 / 走路.

subtleties: In 骑车 the 车 is a bicycle (or an e-bike), not a car.

etymology.text: Ideogrammic compound: 冎 ‘bone’ + 刂 ‘knife’ — cutting apart, hence ‘to separate, other’. Some linguists explain the sense ‘don’t’ as a contraction of 不要.

funFacts: Some linguists think 别 ‘don’t’ is 不要 bú yào said fast — bu-yao → bié.
pitfalls: 别 is only for commands and requests; a plain ‘not’ is 不: 他不走 ‘he isn’t going’, but 别走！ ‘don’t go!’.
别 + verb + 了 means ‘stop …-ing’: 别等了 ‘stop waiting’ (了, S14).
subtleties: 别 is more colloquial than 不要; both stand right before the verb, after the subject if there is one: 你别走.
